thread:
alex: heads-up — saw a ~12% p99 spike on Llama2-13B chat traffic after the kernel-selector change this morning. Only reproducible on sessions with long system prompts + short user turns. attaching brief profile dump.
jamie: ugh. which kernel path is being picked? auto-fused vs fallback?
ravi: looks like auto-fused path (fused-attn-32h) is chosen even when head_dim==64 (model reported as 32 heads but hidden-size metadata inconsistent). selector heuristic matched on "heads" only, not on head_dim align / rope_theta scale. nvprof shows extra memcpy + small-kernel overheads.
maria: can you paste the nvprof snippet? and sample request shape?
alex: nvprof snippet: \n```\nGPU time: fused_attn_kernel 0.82ms\nGPU time: fallback_attn 0.11ms\nTotal tokens: 8\nMemcpy HtoD: 0.45ms\n```\nrequest: prefix 1024 tokens (system), generation chunk 8 tokens, chat-template includes role markers. selector log: picked fused_attn-32h because model_config.heads==32. hidden_size reported 8192 elsewhere.
jamie: that explains it — fused kernel optimized for packed 32h/256hd-per-head; if head_dim mismatch we get unaligned loads and extra memcpy to pack buffers. selector needs to verify head_dim % vector_width == 0.
ravi: also noticed rope_theta defaulting to 0.1 from the loader for this model; earlier prod used 0.08. RoPE scaling affects our prefetch heuristics (KV cache layout changes leading to different memory stride). when prefetch runs it touches pages that cause TLB pressure for the fused kernel.
maria: proposed quick fixes: 1) selector stronger validation: require head_dim % lane_width == 0 and hidden_size consistency 2) prefetch disable for requests with large prefix and short remainder 3) add rope_theta tolerance check and fall back to conservative kernel.
alex: small config draft (please sanity-check):\n```\n"kernel_selector": {\n  "require_headdim_align": true,\n  "headdim_lane_width": 32,\n  "rope_theta_tolerance": 0.02,\n  "prefetch": {\n    "min_remaining_tokens": 16,\n    "disable_on_large_prefix": true\n  }\n}\n```\njamie: looks fine. I suggest headdim_lane_width=16 first (safer) and flip to 32 after canary. also add a soft-fallback metric so we avoid noisy rollbacks.
ravi: agree. add metric name: "kernel_mismatch_prefetch_fallbacks" and emit selector reasons in traces.
maria: testing plan: canary on 10% of traffic (dedicated slot) for 1 hour; collect p50/p90/p99 and kernel-path distribution. regression threshold p99 < +3%.
perf-bot: running canary: traffic slice=10%, duration=1h, collect=[p50,p90,p99,kernel_path_ratio,memcpy_ms] — job queued.
alex: one more nuance — chat templates with role prefixes shrink the effective generation length making batching heuristics pick smaller batching windows; combined with fused kernel penalties this amplifies the regression. we should detect chat-template heavy sessions and prefer fallback kernel when generation_chunk < 12.
jamie: implement rule: if chat_template==true and gen_chunk < 12 and prefix_tokens > 512 => prefer fallback_kernel.
ravi: I'll instrument a small microbenchmark to reproduce locally: create a synthetic session with prefix 1024, gen chunk 8, head_dim mismatch and compare fused vs fallback. will push results here.
maria: thanks. after canary, if stable we'll promote and add a small note to runtime changelog about head-dim alignment and rope_theta sensitivity.
alex: fine — I'll open the runtime PR with the config changes and the selector logging. tagging @jamie @ravi for review.
jamie: review ack. will add the trace emission.
ravi: local microbench shows fused path regressed 11.7% p99, fallback path stable. will attach gist after upload.
alex: thanks all. follow-ups: PR #4572, perf job ID 335555-CANARY-1. we'll reconvene if canary fails. :thumbsup:
